governance.note: ONE lever: replace the placeholder MISO reference-price seam limits (free import to the 7300/4000/3000 MW nameplate interface rating on all three borders) with a MEASURED per-seam EIA-930 BA-to-BA net-import DELIVERABILITY envelope. THE MEASURED INPUT: data/raw/eia-930-interchange/MISO interchange hourly.parquet — the EIA-930 INTERCHANGE (directed BA-to-BA) product for the MISO BA, 2023-2025, columns (diba, mw [EIA sign: + = MISO exports to the DIBA], local_time); its per-year net totals reconstruct the EIA-930 MISO Total Interchange exactly (-37.91/-23.05/-18.96 TWh). For each model seam, constants.MISO_SEAM_DIBA maps the DIBAs that physically cross its border (PJM seam <- {PJM, IESO/Ontario}; SPP seam <- {SWPP, SPA}; South seam <- {SOCO, TVA, AECI, LGEE, SIKE}; Manitoba MHEB EXCLUDED -> the separate firm-hydro block). eia_loader.measured_seam_import_envelope takes the per-(month x hour-of-day) p90 of the seam's summed measured NET IMPORT (-sum over its DIBAs), clipped at 0; transmission.inject_miso_seam_flow_limit scales each seam's import-band availability to that ceiling (one-sided: export bands keep their priced economics). NOT A RESIDUAL FIT (rule #11/#12): the envelope is computed from the directed-flow series BEFORE any LP runs; the p90 is a deliverability-headroom choice (the upper envelope minus the top ~10% transient/loop-flow hours, matching measured_interchange_envelope's default and the interface-limit duration convention), chosen on transfer-capability grounds, NOT tuned to MISO's net-MWh target; the modeled seam price still sets the typical hour within the ceiling, and a seam MISO net-exports over (SPP/South) clips toward ~0 import while its export direction stays economic. NOT PINNED TO ACTUALS (rule #12): it caps the GROSS per-seam DIRECTED transfer (a physical ATC/transfer-capability characteristic, reproducible for a forward year and flow-responsive), it does NOT inject the net-interchange residual nor force the model's net flow onto the measured net. The CAISO measured_corridor_flow_envelope keeper pattern, generalized ISO-agnostically. RESULT: the diagnosed structural over-import is corrected on the import-level-dominated years -- net interchange (EIA +=export) 2023 -71.9->-47.9 (actual -37.9), 2024 -49.8->-25.1 (actual -23.1, near-exact, RMSE 826 MW, import-hrs 90.5 vs 90.9%) -- and gas+coal RECOVER in merit order exactly as predicted (2024 gas 168.7->229.0 = +60 TWh toward EIA-923 257.8; coal 150.4->164.0 toward 175). The faithful cap EXPOSES (does not cause) the now-isolated remaining misses, each a SEPARATE lever (see exceptions): 2025 coal over-run (model long -> exports), PJM neighbor-price over-anchoring in cheap-gas 2024, and the flat Manitoba firm-block level. No outage change: the historic CAMPD unit-outage overlay (exogenous availability events) is unchanged and remains the only measured-availability input.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible end-to-end: (1) the directed-flow parquet is filtered from the EIA-930 sixMonthFiles EIA930_INTERCHANGE_{2023,2024,2025}_{Jan_Jun,Jul_Dec}.csv (Balancing Authority=='MISO' rows); (2) measured_seam_import_envelope('MISO', year, 8760) returns the three seam ceilings (p90, clip>=0), None for any forecast year / unmapped ISO (forecast byte-identical); (3) the LP run log prints 'reference-price seam import capped at measured EIA-930 BA-to-BA deliverability envelope (p90; ...)'. Tests: tests/test_miso_seam_flow_limit.py (envelope scope/clip; per-seam import availability == clipped envelope; export bands untouched; no-op off scope) all pass. Per-seam model-vs-measured net import (positive=import, scratchpad verify): 2023 PJM +31.7 vs +40.9 / SPP +5.9 vs +1.0 / South -1.9 vs -9.4; 2024 PJM +8.4 vs +32.2 / SPP +4.5 vs -0.4 / South -0.1 vs -11.8; 2025 PJM -20.8 vs +28.0 / SPP +6.4 vs +1.0 / South -7.0 vs -9.0. Gas check (the C2 rank-1 guardrail): MISO delivered gas is the measured F923 plant-level fuel cost overlay + Henry-Hub trajectory ($2.54/$2.19/$3.52), unchanged by this lever; 2025 model gas (208.0) already matches EIA-923 (207.6), so the 2025 net miss is the coal offer level, not gas basis. P2 commitment off (meta.passes=[P1], MISO default). Solved per-year to separate out-dirs (16 GB OOM on the 3-year per-plant LP) and merged (scratchpad/merge_year_bundles.py); per-year == combined (no cross-year dependency).

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion on this run is a genuine MODEL MISS to fix in a later lever, NOT an accepted measured-input limitation, so none is entered as a ledger exception (which would wrongly reclassify a FAIL to an ACCEPTED-MEASURED-INPUT-LIMITATION caveat). The determination is therefore NOT-YET with the misses left as honest FAILs (the same posture as the prior keeper miso11). For the record, the now-ISOLATED misses and their (separate) next levers: (1) C2 sysvol 2025 gas -15% / coal +23.8% = the dear-gas COAL OVER-RUN (model coal 237.7 vs 201 EIA-923; model gas already ~exact at 208.0 vs 207.6) -> coal offer / PRB passthrough, NOT the import level (this seam cap correctly EXPOSES the coal length by removing the phantom SPP/South imports that masked it). (2) C1 fuelmix CC_REGULAR over / CT_PEAKER & COAL_BIT under (2023/2024) = the CT-peaker merit under-gen + slight coal under, which recover further once the scarcity tail exists and the 2025 coal level is fixed. (3) C3c price tail 0 scarcity hours = no ORDC/scarcity mechanism in MISO yet (inherited from miso11). (4) C5a CO2 -12.6/-9.1% (2023/2024) = downstream of the gas/coal under. (5) C5b storage 2025 +1344% = the over-export length distorts the arbitrage spread. Also adjacent, not part of this lever's mechanism: the PJM seam UNDER-imports in cheap-gas 2024 (model +8.4 vs measured +32.2; the cap is NOT binding -> the per-year PJM HR anchor 13.49 over-prices the PJM hub, a neighbor-price item) and the flat 1400 MW Manitoba firm block (12.3 TWh/yr) over-imports vs measured MHEB 5.4/3.0/-1.0 (settled miso_firm_imports level). None of these is closable by an adder/haircut/pin/rescale to a residual (rule #12).
